chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 3
subject: english

questions.question: 'He would certainly not countenance it.' The underlined word 'countenance' means:
questions.explanation: 'Countenance' as a transitive verb means to accept, sanction, tolerate, or permit as acceptable.

questions.question: The cat jumped ___ the counter. Choose the correct preposition:
questions.explanation: 'Off' describes movement away from a raised surface or platform.

questions.question: 'Writing an email is an exchange of ideas.' The underlined word 'Writing' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Writing' is an -ing verbal noun functioning as the subject of the sentence, which characterizes a gerund.

questions.question: A long, grand narrative poem recounting the heroic deeds of legendary figures is a/an:
questions.explanation: Epic poetry (e.g., The Odyssey, Paradise Lost) is an elevated narrative centered on monumental deeds and national heroes.

questions.question: 'Whether you like it or not, you have to go to bed now.' The underlined clause is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Whether you like it or not' is a dependent adverbial clause of concession modifying the predicate.

questions.question: Excessive pride and dangerous arrogance that leads to the downfall of a tragic hero is called:
questions.explanation: Hubris is the classical literary term for reckless self-confidence and insolent pride in tragic literature.

questions.question: Which one of the following sentences has the use of a transitional device of contrast?

options.A: The people who play basketball are more fit.
options.B: John is tall but Adam is taller.
options.C: Firstly she prepared dough then, she baked pizza.
options.D: Nobody paid attention to her speech for there was nuisance in the hall.

questions.explanation: 'But' functions as an adversative transitional conjunction introducing a contrasting comparative statement.

questions.question: Which pair has the same analogy relationship as between Hydrogen and Gas?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is an elemental substance that naturally exists in gaseous state; Mercury is an element that uniquely exists as a liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: Which one of the sentences contains a Rhetorical Question?

options.A: Will no one tell me what she sings?

questions.explanation: Wordsworth's line from 'The Solitary Reaper' is posed for evocative emotional resonance rather than eliciting factual replies.

questions.question: 'The man was injured in an accident, but he recovered soon.' It is a/an:
questions.explanation: Consists of two independent clauses linked by the coordinating conjunction 'but'.

questions.question: 'If they had not come, I would have been disappointed.' This sentence belongs to:
questions.explanation: Third conditional expresses an unreal past condition ('had not come') with a past counterfactual result ('would have been').

questions.question: Which of the following lines exemplifies synecdoche?

options.A: If you can force your heart and nerve and sinew
options.B: If you can dream and not make your dream your master
options.C: Twisted by knaves to make a trap for fools
options.D: And risk it on one turn of pitch-and-toss

questions.explanation: Physical bodily organs ('heart, nerve, sinew') are selected to stand as parts representing the entirety of human determination and energy.

questions.question: 'Julia works at a pet store and owns dogs, cats, and rabbits.' What can we deduce about Julia?
questions.explanation: Voluntarily surrounding oneself with domestic companions across workplace and home signifies an ardent affinity for pets.

questions.question: 'Broken images is a famous poem in literature.' The word 'Broken' is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Broken' is the past participle form of 'break' functioning as an attributive adjective modifying 'images'.

questions.question: Which sentence has the use of a transitive verb?

options.A: Wassay takes a cup of coffee in the morning.
options.B: She is an active student of our class.

questions.explanation: 'Takes' is transitive because its action transfers directly to the direct object ('a cup of coffee').

questions.question: 'I met the teacher when I reached the college.' The underlined clause is a/an:
questions.explanation: 'When I reached the college' contains its own subject and verb, modifying 'met' as an adverbial clause of time.

questions.question: Which sentence is correctly in the future perfect tense?

options.A: When the sun rises we will have left.
options.B: When the sun rises we will leave.
options.C: When the sun rises we had left.
options.D: When the sun rises we will have been left.

questions.explanation: Future perfect ('will have left') indicates that an action will be completed before a specific future time or event.

questions.question: 'The police will have filed the case.' The correct passive voice transformation is:

options.A: The case will have been filed by the police.
options.B: The case shall have been filed by the police.
options.C: The case will have filed by the police.
options.D: The case would have been filed by the police.

questions.explanation: Future perfect active 'will have + V3' systematically converts to passive 'will have been + V3'.

questions.question: Which sentence has the use of a Noun clause?

options.A: The boy on the roof is flying a kite.
options.B: She was saddened by what she had read.
options.C: Baking is one of my favourite hobbies.
options.D: We got late because it was raining heavily.

questions.explanation: 'What she had read' is a noun clause functioning as the object of the preposition 'by'.

questions.question: A tragic flaw or misjudgment in character that brings about the protagonist's fall is called:
questions.explanation: Hamartia is Aristotle's Poetics term for the internal character defect leading directly to catastrophic doom.
